story.heading: Our Story
story.body: Did you know that someone can start from nothing and build something truly meaningful? This belief inspired the founding of AGILE – Audit, Advisory, Governance & Leadership Excellence in 2026. Co‑founded by Chartered Accountants — among them Claudine Simo Mamo, a CEMAC‑certified Chartered Accountant and Fellow of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) — AGILE embodies the collective expertise of its partners while reflecting Claudine’s 37 years of leadership in finance and accounting across the CEMAC region. Mme Simo joined Agile to mentor young professionals, building leadership capacity, ownership, and accountability within teams. As a strategic advisor to banks, insurance companies, microfinance institutions and asset management, she strengthens financial systems, ensures regulatory compliance (OHADA, COBAC, CIMA, COSUMAF), and drives performance optimisation, particularly in agro-industry, banks and microfinance structuring. Her vision is clear: show that sustainable success comes from strong foundations, discipline, and continuous growth. At Agile, we secure value, empower growth, and build trust – proving that meaningful futures are forged from humble beginnings, one strategic step at a time. At Agile, we lead audit and assurance services in CEMAC and beyond, committed to securing value, empowering growth, and building trust for institutions, shareholders, and agro-industrial leaders in Cameroon.

founderBio.heading: Claudine Simo Mamo, Founder and Managing Partner
founderBio.body: Claudine Simo Mamo is a CEMAC-certified Chartered Accountant and Fellow of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), with over 37 years of experience in audit, accounting, and advisory across Central Africa. Her career reflects both discipline and progression. She began her career in education in 1988, before transitioning into project management and later joining ECA IN 2012, where she built her expertise over time. As the firm evolved within the Ernst & Young (EY) network, she grew into leadership roles, serving as Associate Director and Head of Audit for Cameroon and Chad IN 2013, leading complex engagements across banking, insurance, asset management, agro-industry and utilities. In 2023, she reached a key milestone in her journey when she became a Partner at ECA S.A., where she led audit, statutory audit, accounting, and advisory services for major institutions across the region. Today, she operates as an Independent Chartered Accountant and Founder and Managing Partner of AGILE (Audit, Advisory, Governance & Leadership Excellence), where she supports financial institutions and growing organisations in strengthening their systems, improving governance, and building sustainable performance. At this stage of her career, her focus goes beyond numbers. She is deeply committed to developing people, mentoring young professionals, building a culture of responsibility, and contributing to organisations where individuals are empowered to grow into leadership. This commitment is reflected in her active leadership within the accounting profession, where she serves as a Member of ONECCA (National Order of Chartered Accountants of Cameroon), sitting on the Council as Deputy Treasurer, and as a Distinguished Fellow Member of ACCA (FCCA)

faqs.a: Audit and assurance services assess the accuracy, reliability and compliance of financial information and business processes. An audit provides an independent review of records and controls, while assurance gives stakeholders confidence that the information is credible, complete and prepared to the required standard. Together they help businesses improve transparency, reduce risk and strengthen trust.

faqs.q: What are audit and assurance services?
faqs.a: These include independent checks of financial statements, internal controls, compliance and operational processes. They help organisations meet legal and regulatory requirements, identify weaknesses and improve decision making. Common examples include statutory audits, internal audits, compliance reviews and limited assurance engagements. They build confidence among investors, regulators, lenders and management.

faqs.q: What are the main types of audits?
faqs.a: The main types are financial audits, compliance audits, operational audits and forensic audits. Financial audits review statements for accuracy. Compliance audits check whether rules and regulations are followed. Operational audits assess efficiency and effectiveness. Forensic audits investigate suspected fraud or misconduct. Each serves a different purpose in protecting business integrity.

faqs.a: SYSCOHADA is the harmonised accounting system used across OHADA member states in West and Central Africa. It provides common rules for financial reporting, making accounts more consistent, transparent and comparable across businesses and countries. It helps organisations comply with regional accounting requirements while improving the quality and reliability of financial information.

Collateral security is an asset a borrower pledges to a lender to secure a loan. If the borrower fails to repay, the lender can use the asset to recover the debt. It reduces lending risk and can help businesses or individuals access finance more easily. Common examples include land, vehicles, machinery, inventory or other valuable property.

ESG audits are independent reviews of an organisation's environmental, social and governance practices. They assess whether policies, reporting and performance are accurate, responsible and aligned with sustainability standards. ESG audits help businesses identify risks, improve transparency and strengthen trust with investors, regulators and stakeholders.

faqs.q: What are common risk assessment tools?

The right tool depends on your sector, regulatory environment and the level of detail you need for reporting and decisions.

faqs.a: Budgeting and monitoring is the process of planning income and expenditure, then tracking actual performance against the approved budget. It helps organisations control costs, spot variances early and make informed decisions. In practice it supports better cash flow management, stronger accountability and more accurate forecasting.

faqs.q: What is the purpose of tax compliance in Cameroon?
faqs.a: Tax compliance ensures individuals and businesses meet their legal tax obligations, file accurately and pay on time. It helps avoid penalties, supports government revenue collection and strengthens transparency. Good tax compliance also improves business credibility, reduces regulatory risk and supports long term financial stability.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for tax compliance?
faqs.a: Tax compliance is the responsibility of both the business and its management. Directors, finance teams, accountants and tax advisers all play a role in ensuring accurate records, correct filings and timely payments. In larger organisations responsibility may be shared, but the ultimate duty remains with the taxpayer and its leadership.

performance.keywords: budgeting and monitoring, tax compliance Cameroon, compliance services, accounting engineering

faqs.q: What are two major methods of asset valuation?
faqs.a: Two major methods are the cost method and the market value method. The cost method values an asset based on its original purchase or replacement cost. The market value method estimates what the asset would sell for in the open market. These methods are widely used for business planning, financial reporting, succession planning and investment decisions.

Heritage assets are items of historical, cultural, artistic, scientific or environmental importance. They are often held for public benefit and preserved for future generations rather than mainly for commercial use. They can be difficult to value because of their uniqueness, but still require proper recognition, control and disclosure in financial reporting where applicable.

Business succession planning prepares a company for leadership or ownership transfer when an owner retires, becomes unavailable or exits. It helps maintain stability, protect value and avoid disruption. Good succession planning supports continuity, tax efficiency and long term growth by ensuring the right people and structures are in place.

faqs.q: What manager training supports employee growth?
faqs.a: Useful manager training includes leadership development, performance management, communication skills, financial awareness and team coaching. The best programmes help managers improve decision making, support employee development and drive productivity. Good manager training is practical, relevant to your sector and focused on real workplace results rather than theory.

faqs.q: What training is best for managers?
faqs.a: The best training depends on the role, but leadership, communication, delegation, conflict resolution and financial management are among the most valuable. Managers also benefit from strategic thinking, people management and compliance training. Effective management training improves confidence, accountability and team performance.

Governance training is structured learning that helps directors, board members and senior leaders understand their responsibilities, regulatory duties and oversight roles. It covers accountability, compliance, risk management, ethics and internal controls, strengthening board performance, decision making and organisational leadership.

At AGILE, we provide the technical architecture required to professionalize your core operations, mitigate systemic risks, and drive sustainable, tech-enabled growth.

faqs.a: A statutory audit (CAC) is an annual legal audit required for certain entities, including banks, insurers, microfinance institutions and listed companies. It verifies the reliability of financial information and compliance with applicable laws and standards. Across CEMAC and beyond, statutory audits strengthen transparency, accountability and stakeholder confidence.

Accounting systems diagnostics is a review of an organisation's financial organisation, audit trail and the reliability of its financial statements. It helps identify weaknesses in accounting processes, internal controls and reporting structures. It is essential for improving accuracy, strengthening governance and supporting better decisions.

Contractual audits are independent reviews for specific transactions or engagements, such as acquisition due diligence, project audits and limited reviews. They help organisations assess risk, confirm data reliability and make informed commercial decisions, particularly valuable during investments, partnerships and major projects.

faqs.q: What is SYSCOHADA audit and certification?
faqs.a: SYSCOHADA audit and certification is a specialised service for agro industrial complexes operating under the OHADA framework. It ensures compliance with harmonised accounting standards and supports accurate reporting, helping agro industrial businesses strengthen performance, secure assets and improve credibility with investors, lenders and regulators.

faqs.q: What does collateral security mean in agricultural financing?
faqs.a: Collateral security refers to the legal protection given to lenders through pledged assets in agricultural financing. It helps secure loans and reduce credit risk. Our expertise in securities law supports reliable collateral arrangements that protect both lenders and borrowers while improving access to finance.

faqs.q: What is legal structuring in agro industry?
faqs.a: Legal structuring in agro industry involves drafting value chain contracts and public and private partnership agreements that support commercial relationships and protect business interests. It ensures arrangements are clear, enforceable and aligned with the OHADA framework, improving stability, compliance and long term value creation.

faqs.q: What is an ESG compliance audit?
faqs.a: An ESG compliance audit reviews how environmental, social and governance risks are identified, managed and reported. It helps organisations improve sustainability reporting, strengthen accountability and meet stakeholder expectations. In agro industry and other sectors it supports responsible growth and long term resilience.

COBAC compliance services support banks and microfinance institutions in meeting banking regulatory requirements across CEMAC. These include risk mapping, stress testing, liquidity management and operational risk prevention, helping institutions strengthen prudential control, reduce exposure and improve financial stability.

faqs.q: What are CIMA actuarial and compliance services?
faqs.a: CIMA actuarial and compliance services support insurers with technical provisions review, solvency analysis and actuarial pricing. They help insurers meet regulatory expectations, manage risk and maintain financial soundness, essential for compliance, accurate reporting and long term stability.

Succession planning is the process of structuring and securing the transfer of business or personal assets over time. It includes asset valuation, heritage diagnostics and tax secured transmission, helping protect wealth, reduce conflict and ensure continuity across generations or ownership changes.
